gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the bridge unsafe, but it was also far too narrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the bridge unsafe' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: Only later ___ we realise what he had done.
gaps.explanation: 'Only later did we realise' — inverted past simple.

gaps.sentence: To such an extent ___ prices risen that buyers withdrew.
gaps.hint: To such an extent + past perfect
gaps.explanation: To such an extent had prices risen that… — emphatic result.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ the villagers suspect that the mine would ever reopen.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did the villagers suspect' — they had no idea.

gaps.sentence: Only by practising daily ___ you improve your fluency.
gaps.explanation: Only by doing X will you… — future inversion after only by.

gaps.sentence: Only later ___ it occur to her that the letter had been a forgery.
gaps.explanation: 'Only later' at the front inverts with do-support: did it occur to her.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ refunds be given after this date.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances will refunds be given' — inverted modal passive.

gaps.sentence: Reluctant ___ she was to intervene, the referee stopped the match.
gaps.explanation: Fronted adjective + though/as + subject is emphatic concession: Reluctant though she was…
